severity_name: HEAVY SLOP WARNING — ARCHIVAL FALSIFICATION ADVISORY
headline: HEAVY SLOP WARNING: SEPIA-TONED COUNTERFEIT-HISTORY FRONT SWEEPS THE FACEBOOK DELTA AS FABRICATED VINTAGE PHOTOGRAPHS DOCUMENT EVENTS, PERSONS, AND ENTIRE CENTURIES THAT NEVER OCCURRED
advisory: A slow-moving system of counterfeit archival imagery has settled over the lowlands, depositing artificially aged photographs captioned with phrases such as 'colorized, 1908' and 'rare footage they don't want you to see.' Residents are reminded that a photograph exhibiting six-fingered laborers, buildings that predate their own architecture, and a soft golden haze covering all of recorded time is not a lost treasure of the National Archive. The Service advises against sharing any image whose caption ends in 'why don't they teach this in schools.' We do not, in fact, teach it in schools.

regional_outlook.conditions: Dense sepia fog throughout the day, with fabricated 'rare photos' pooling in community groups. Comment sections showing heavy accumulation of 'God bless the past' with zero visibility of a source.
Persistent drizzle of impossible antique architecture and 'historical fashion' that no fabric has ever supported. Repinning likely to spread the front inland.
Gusty reply-quote conditions as counterfeit history collides with weary corrections. Debris field of 'this is fake, actually' expected to be ignored by nightfall.
Forwarded-chain surge, mostly overnight. Subject lines reading 'INCREDIBLE — you won't believe #7' accumulating in family folders.
Scattered 'lost recordings' of orchestras that were never assembled. Otherwise mild, with a faint hiss of artificial vinyl crackle added in post.

specimen.status: Abundant and breeding; now the dominant species in the Facebook Delta wetlands.
specimen.habitat: Community history groups, nostalgia pages, and any feed where the word 'colorized' has been sighted in the last decade.
specimen.field_marks: An unnaturally uniform golden-brown wash across the entire frame; hands rendered as a democratic negotiation between four and seven fingers; signage in a language resembling English viewed through a screen door; and a caption asserting a precise year with the confidence of a species that has never met a calendar.
specimen.call: Colorized, 1874. Sadly, no photos like this survive today. Share to honor the forgotten.
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine digitized archival scan. A real archival photograph carries a catalog number, an institution, and a photographer who existed; the counterfeit carries only a haze, a heartfelt caption, and forty thousand shares from people who love the past more than the facts.

spotter_tip: Zoom in on the hands and the signage. History was blurry, but it could always count to five and spell.
tomorrow: Counterfeit-history front persists into Tuesday, with a developing band of 'AI-restored' celebrity portraits that restore faces to people who never sat for the camera.

confirmed_sighting.report: Faculty experts at Ohio University report that AI slop is flooding social media at a scale of tens of millions of AI-generated images produced daily, with measurable effects on the media landscape and public trust in information. The Service notes the figure is per day, and declines to picture the year.
